identity.name: Norse Greenland
native_names: Eystribyggð and Vestribyggð (the Eastern and Western Settlements)

capitals.name: Brattahlíð (Qassiarsuk)
capitals.note: G1: the Eastern Settlement lay around today's Qaqortoq, at the end of Eiriksfjord, with Brattahlíð as its main farm; Garðar (today's Igaliku) was the bishop's seat from 1126 (the first bishop, Arnaldr, is dated from 1126; the last died in 1378). Greenland had no royal capital; Brattahlíð is Erik the Red's farm and the settlement's centre.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the years before Cliopatria's 1072 shape (Cliopatria draws Greenland in its Viking settlements row for 1000-1071). G1: Erik sailed west in 982 and settlement began after 986 CE; Brattahlíð was founded the spring after his first winter; the page dates neither the Middle nor the Western Settlement, so all three are drawn from the start.

26,128 km2, bbox -52.25..-47.41 E, 60.77..65.15 N. The gazetteer shows the shape covers the Western Settlement (Nuuk, Kapisillit) and the Middle Settlement (Ivittuut) but NOT the Eastern Settlement: Qaqortoq, Narsarsuaq (Brattahlíð), Igaliku (Garðar), Narsaq and Hvalsey fall outside it (its east edge is -47.41E, the Eastern Settlement lies at 45.4-46.1W). G1 puts the Eastern Settlement around today's Qaqortoq, with about 500 of the 620 farms (Western about 95, Middle about 20) and the bishop's seat; it is the heart of the colony. G1 gives no area. The shape should add a 70 km radius round Qaqortoq.

G1: 'the Greenland colony subordinated itself to the Norwegian crown in 1261'. The colony is a Norwegian dependency drawn as its own shape (a lighter tint of Norway); the Western Settlement is still inhabited until about 1350.

ledger.note: c. 986: Erik the Red founds the Eastern Settlement at Brattahlíð. G1: 'The Landnámabók reports that in 982 he sailed west' and settlement began after 986 CE; the founding fleet was 25 ships, of which 14 reached Greenland. 986 is the page's lower bound, not a date it gives; G2 has the Norse presence beginning in the 'late 10th century AD'. The Western and Middle Settlements are undated on both pages and are drawn from the start.

region.text: the Greenland colony, Eastern, Middle and Western Settlements

ledger.note: 1261: the Greenland colony accepts the Norwegian king. G1: 'the Greenland colony subordinated itself to the Norwegian crown in 1261.' G2 agrees: 'in 1261, they accepted the overlordship of the Norwegian king'. The state and its settlements continue as a dependency of Norway; the vassal_start belongs in the Old Kingdom of Norway dossier (counterpart norse-greenland). Reviewer eu-14-e, 2026-10-25: recorded as vassal_start (counterpart old-kingdom-of-norway) instead of rename, so that it mirrors the suzerain's event; the tie lasts to the colony's end in 1408.

region.text: the Western Settlement, about 90 farms near Kapisillit

ledger.note: c. 1350: the Western Settlement is empty. G2: 'The Western Settlement was abandoned around 1350.' G1: in 1350 Ívar Bárðarson sailed there and found no one living; the 1355 expedition under Paul Knutsson found no Norse; G1 allows an abandonment anywhere in 1350-1400.

ledger.note: 1408: the last written record of the Norse in Greenland. G2: 'After a marriage was recorded in 1408, no written records mention the settlers'; G1: a wedding at Hvalsey Church on 14 September 1408 is the last known written record and the guests returned to Iceland in 1410. Neither page dates the colony's end: G1 has the settlements abandoned 'between 1350 and 1500', G2 'defunct by the late 15th century'; 1408 is the last evidence, not a date the pages give for the end.

sources.title: Norse colonization of North America
sources.note: The article Cliopatria names for this row; it covers Vinland and Greenland as a base, gives the Western Settlement's abandonment c. 1350, the 1408 marriage and the 1261 overlordship; no founding date for Greenland.

notes:
DECISION: Norse Greenland is a settler state (986-1261) that became a dependency of the Norwegian crown (1261) and died out unrecorded after the last written record of 1408. Cliopatria's years are 1072-1271 and 1363-1384 with a gap in between (where Greenland sits inside the Old Kingdom of Norway and, wrongly, the Kingdom of Sweden); this dossier fills 986-1408 with new keyframes.
SHAPE ERROR: the 1072 and 1363/1375 shapes omit the Eastern Settlement (Qaqortoq, Brattahlíð, Garðar, Hvalsey): they cover the Western (Nuuk, Kapisillit) and Middle (Ivittuut) areas only, checked with the gazetteer. The Eastern Settlement was most of the colony (G1: about 500 of 620 farms). All keyframes are corrected by adding a 70 km radius round Qaqortoq.
TITLE: Cliopatria's Wikipedia title 'Norse colonization of North America' (Wikidata Q582948) is about Vinland with Greenland as the base (G2); 'Norse settlements in Greenland' (G1) is the right article for this row.
VASSAL RECORD: the 1261 submission is recorded here only as a rename event (G1 'subordinated itself', G2 'accepted the overlordship': a vassal tie, not an annexation). The old-kingdom-of-norway dossier (eu-14-c, repaired) records a gain of Greenland in 1261 with counterpart norse-greenland and draws it in its keyframes from 1261, so its drawing overlaps this one on Greenland for 1261-1397 and its gain has no matching loss here. Preferred fix: that event becomes a vassal_start (and a vassal_end for the colony's end), and Greenland stays this state's land to 1408 as in Cliopatria's own Norse Greenland row (1363-1384 overlaps the Norwegian shape there too). Otherwise this dossier needs a loss at 1261 for old-kingdom-of-norway and no keyframes after it. The reviewer decides; nothing is changed here. The kingdom-of-sweden dossier's 1333-1374 keyframes drop Greenland (flagged there).
NOT ON THE PAGES: the founding of the Western and Middle Settlements, any area figure, the fate of the Eastern Settlement after 1408 beyond 'abandoned between 1350 and 1500' (G1) and 'defunct by the late 15th century' (G2), the Inuit (Thule) arrival, Iceland's relation before 1261. G1 gives two farm counts for the Eastern Settlement (500 and 192). Rulers: none (no ruler list exists).
GAZETTEER names used that the gazetteer lacks: 'Brattahlíð / Qassiarsuk' (61.15N 45.52W, a capital coordinate), 'Garðar / Igaliku' (60.99N 45.43W), 'Hvalsey' (60.9N 45.9W), 'Ivittuut' (61.2N 48.2W): written as Qaqortoq and Nuuk radii. Pages used: 2 of 2. REVIEWER eu-14-e (2026-10-25): the 1261 event was changed from rename to vassal_start with counterpart old-kingdom-of-norway (G1 'subordinated itself', G2 'accepted the overlordship'); the old-kingdom-of-norway side still records a gain and draws Greenland, which its owner must turn into the suzerain's vassal_start.
